question: In its reply to our Question E-001178/20251, the Commission invokes the following as the legal basis for the suspension on 4 March 2022 of funding to all Russian entities under Horizon Europe: – Article 1i of Council Decision 2014/512/CFSP2; – Article 5l of Council Regulation (EU) No 833/20143; – A restrictive eligibility clause in the Work Programme, authorised by Article 22(6) of the Horizon Europe Regulation4.

However, the decision to suspend was taken on 4 March 2022, whereas: – Article 1i was added to Council Decision 2014/512/CFSP5 only on 8 April 2022; – Article 5l was likewise added on 8 April 2022 by Council Regulation (EU) 2022/5766 amending Regulation (EU) No 833/20147; – The Work Programme clause excluding Russia appears to have been approved only on 10 May 2022.
8 Since the suspension decision predates the adoption of these provisions, it is unclear how they could have constituted its legal basis. 1.
Can the Commission specify what legal basis, as of 4 March 2022, conferred upon it the competence to suspend cooperation with all Russian entities?
Does the Commission consider that it has the same legal competence to suspend or restrict Horizon Europe cooperation with Israeli entities, and if not, why not?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.2.2026) 1. On 24 February 2022, the European Council condemned Russia’s military aggression against Ukraine.

The Council of the European Union adopted subsequently far-reaching restrictive measures, including in particular the freezing of funds and economic resources of numerous Russian entities and individuals, as well as prohibitions, among others, to provide support to entities established in Russia with over 50 percent public ownership or control.
In this context, on 4 March 2022, the Commission also announced measures aimed at suspending cooperation with Russian entities under the Horizon Europe programme.

Following the announcement of 4 March 2022 and the adoption of the relevant legal measures, the termination of the participation of Russian entities in new and ongoing EU financed projects, as well as the suspension of payments, has been carried out on a case-bycase assessment, in line with the applicable regulatory framework1. 2.

Regarding Horizon Europe cooperation with Israeli and Russian entities, the legal framework differs. As regards Israeli entities, there are no restrictive measures in place relating to Israel as such (while certain Israeli persons are listed under other sanctions regimes). As regards Russian entities, there was no association agreement concluded similar to the linked Euro-Mediterranean Agreement2 with Israel.

In this respect, the Commission proposal to partially suspend the application of the Horizon Europe association agreement with Israel was based on Articles 2 and 79(2) of the Euro-Mediterranean Agreement.
1 I.e. the applicable EU restrictive measures adopted under Article 29 of the Treaty on the European Union as

well as Article 215 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, notably Council Decision 2014/512/CFSP and Council Regulation (EU) No 833/2014. 2 http://data.europa.eu/eli/agree_internation/2000/384/2013-07-01.
